headline: Highest risk is low: no shared I/O or network path is documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes a shared communication channel, filesystem surface, or clipboard/MCP bridge. Agent A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; agent B also shows no I/O surfaces. With no documented path for A’s outputs to reach B, prompt injection is provably blocked from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared paste/clipboard bridges.
Do not connect them to a shared MCP server without provenance tracking.
requires-engineering: add explicit content provenance tags on any future handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, both report network egress as none, and no shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented. A cannot leak via network, and B likewise has no documented path to transmit context. The pairwise leakage pathway is therefore not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted network egress, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF a shared workspace is introduced and sensitive files are placed there, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation if a shared filesystem is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write or network capabilities, while B can install packages but has no documented filesystem write surface or concurrency model. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Uncertainty remains because the profiles are sparse, so the safer choice is low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF either agent is run under an orchestrator without locking and both mutate shared state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not grant both agents write access to the same path.
Run package installation in an isolated environment.
requires-engineering: add file locks before any shared mutable resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static repository of Python resources, not an active producer of facts or actions, and B is a customer-support agent with no documented downstream action authority. Without a documented handoff, B cannot be shown to treat A’s output as authoritative. The interaction is therefore weak and best classified low.
conditions: IF A’s content is later fed into B as trusted instructions, cascading error risk increases.
IF B is configured to execute actions from retrieved content, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not pipe A’s repository text directly into B as instructions.
Require human review before B acts on retrieved content.
requires-engineering: add verification checks for any future retrieval-to-action flow.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. A and B both show empty data-class fields and no compliance-specific surfaces, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to score. The other agent is not separately cited because the same absence is the relevant fact for both.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced, compliance must be re-scored.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy, verify alignment before use.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency rules before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if regulated data is later introduced.
